transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42m
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marta Lopez (Brightside, Head of ML), Ethan Cole (Brightside, Platform Eng), Sandra Kim (Brightside, CTO)

Summary:
Weekly POC check-in focused on cost/unit economics: tokens per dollar, caching savings observed in last 72h, and batching tradeoffs. Customer reported edge tail-latency on 512 token prompts; Redwood recommended config tweaks and follow-up benchmarks. Agreed next steps: 24h caching benchmark, SE deep dive for tail latency, updated pricing scenarios.

Topics:
- recent pilot metrics (tokens/sec/$, avg tok/sec, cache hit rate)
- KV/prefix caching behavior and observed savings
- batching policy: micro-batch vs continuous batching tradeoffs
- latency tail and mitigation options (model variants, routing)
- security/deployment constraints (data residency question raised)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we just have, uh, a tight agenda today, cost per unit focus. Marta, do you want to kick off with what you saw this week?
[00:24] Marta: yeah sure, um, thanks Jordan. So we ran the new canopy prompts over the weekend and saw around a 23% reduction in tokens/sec/$ when caching was enabled but the tail latency spiked a bit on a subset of requests so - - I can share the dashboard.
[00:48] Priya: when you say tail, can you quantify, like p95 p99?
[00:53] Marta: yeah, p95 is stable around 210ms but p99 jumped to 1.8s on the 512-token flows, which is not what we expected, most 128/256 flows are fine.
[01:12] Ethan: just to add, those were real user flows with some long QA style prompts, also we had a couple of sudden bursts from a downstream job which may have caused KV cache invalidations.
[01:26] Priya: okay that makes sense, sometimes the cache key shaping plus burst evictions can cause misses and then we backfill the KV which creates a small org — uh — spike, we call that a cache backfill tail.
[01:45] Jordan: and that relates to batching too, like if requests are micro-batched timeouts can appear if the batch waits, or conversely, if we force immediate single-item dispatch costs goes up.
[01:58] Sandra: real quick, what's the delta in cost if we move to single request mode vs the continuous batching you recommend?
[02:06] Priya: rough ballpark from our internal bench — single-item gives you lower latency for warm-core requests but cost per token is ~30-40% higher because you lose the multiplication effect of batching. Continuous batching with a 10ms gather window usually gets the sweet spot.
[02:28] Marta: can Redwood run a 24h sustained test with the exact prompt mix? We want to see tokens/sec/$ over production-like noise.
[02:36] Jordan: yes we can, Priya will run a 24-hour benchmark with KV cache on/off and with 5/10/20ms gather windows so you get tokens/sec/$ across configurations.
[02:47] Ethan: perfect, also can you show us the exact kernel selection metrics? We saw sometimes the runtime switches to a slower path for longer sequences and I want to confirm it's not a model mismatch.
[03:00] Priya: yeah we'll grab the kernel selection trace, altho note the profiler has some sampling noise so we'll send a couple runs.
[03:12] Marta: small thing, we noticed the docs mention "KV cash" in an older guide and it confused a couple of infra engineers, little typos but harmless.
[03:22] Jordan: oh thanks, will fix that in the guide.
[03:25] Sandra: on security, quick check, we still need confirmation about data residency for PHI workloads. If we need a Private deployment that's a different engagement.
[03:37] Jordan: understoood, for PHI we'd recommend Private or a Dedicated with the right controls; I'll share the data residency checklist and the template SAML SSO doc.
[03:49] Ethan: one more operational note — we're seeing a few 503s tied to our LB reconfig during bursts; curious if Redwood has suggestions for graceful fallback or pre-warmed capacity.
[04:02] Priya: we can set up automatic fallbacks to a lower-cost compatible model during capacity pressure, or use dedicated reserved pool with small burst capacity. There's also a per-route fallback policy you can configure.
[04:16] Marta: what's the unit economics effect of using a fallback model? Like do we lose too much quality?
[04:23] Priya: it depends on the workload. For QA prompts top-K shift is small for the 3B->7B family so you might be fine, but for summarization we always recommend an eval set to detect regressions. Redwood Optimize can run continuous evals and raise an alert if quality drifts.
[04:44] Jordan: back to numbers — your last 72h summary that you sent shows cache hit rate at 62% and average tokens per call 420, is that still accurate?
[04:56] Marta: yes, that's right, hit rate varies a lot by user cohort, power users have 78% hit rate, casuals 45%.
[05:07] Ethan: is there a recommendation for key shaping? Our keys are entire prompt hashes which might be too coarse.
[05:13] Priya: depending on your prompt patterns you'd usually shard by prompt template + user id prefix, avoid ephemeral session tokens in the key. Also consider prefix caching for common boilerplate.
[05:27] Marta: we tried prefix but then bumped into some policy mismatch, i'll send the example.
[05:33] Jordan: alright let's walk through the three config knobs we think matter: batch window, cache TTL & key shape, and model variant routing.
[05:44] Priya: for batch window we recommended testing 5/10/20ms, as Jordan mentioned; for TTL try 60s vs 300s to see how bursty evictions behave; and for routing we can do a canary route to a smaller model for non-critical endpoints.
[06:00] Sandra: can the routing be A/B so we can measure quality delta?
[06:04] Priya: yes, canary and A/B are both supported in the deployment config, and console will show token/cost breakdown per route.
[06:12] Ethan: curious — what's the tokens/sec/$ we should expect on a balanced workload for a 13B-like open model on your hosted tier?
[06:20] Jordan: ballpark, on a hosted inference cluster with continuous batching and cache effective, you might see ~70-120k tokens/sec per $1 depending on sequence length and quantization; for 13B-family models toward the lower side, 50-80k. These are back-of-envelope numbers.
[06:40] Marta: that aligns with our internal roughs but we need the concrete numbers from the 24h test.
[06:45] Jordan: yes, Priya will post the bench result and a spreadsheet mapping tokens/sec/$ by config.
[06:52] Marta: on the cost side, we have procurement constraint — can't exceed our projected $Xk/mo for this pilot, so if we need Dedicated that changes the seat.
[07:03] Jordan: understood, in the pricing sheet we'll show both hosted and reserved capacity scenarios; reserved lowers unit cost but requires commit.
[07:13] Ethan: any quick wins we can do this week to reduce spend without much risk?
[07:17] Priya: enable prefix caching on the top 10 templates and try the 10ms batch window, that usually yields 10-20% immediate gains. Also tune prompt length by trimming boilerplate and recommending summarization heuristics.
[07:31] Marta: we're already pruning some prompts, will share the list.
[07:34] Jordan: I'll also attach the Redwood caching guide and a playbook for batching in Slack after the call.
[07:40] Sandra: regarding compliance, do you have SOC2 and ISO docs we can give to security?
[07:45] Jordan: yes, i'll push the security pack link. If you require encryption at rest with customer-managed keys, that is supported on Private or on Dedicated with KMS integrations.
[07:57] Ethan: FYI, our infra folks prefer a VPC peering approach, is that supported?
[08:02] Priya: yes VPC peering or private link are both options for Private/Dedicated; we can follow up with network team to map ports and firewall rules.
[08:12] Marta: ok circling back to tail latency — what's the triage path?
[08:15] Priya: we'll triage traces, check for cache-miss correlation, kernel selection slow path, and whether the request coincided with a node GC or rebalancing. We'll need the trace ids and a 30m window around incidents.
[08:31] Ethan: will collect logs and share them in a secure bucket with Redwood SE.
[08:36] Jordan: good, any other blockers?
[08:38] Sandra: just decision on Private vs Hosted for PHI; we'll talk to legal.
[08:43] Jordan: noted.
[08:45] Marta: one more question — how do you measure tokens/sec/$ in multi-model routing? We have a mix of 7B and 13B.
[08:55] Priya: console shows per-model token counts and cost breakdown; our optimize engine can also suggest per-route model assignments based on historical latency and token churn. We'll include a per-route sheet in the deliverable.
[09:10] Jordan: ok let's recap next steps — Priya 24h bench, Jordan pricing sheet, Ethan logs, Marta confirm success criteria. Any objections?
[09:21] Marta: none.
[09:22] Sandra: nope.
[09:23] Jordan: great thanks everyone. We'll meet same time next week.

End of transcript.
